title: Phrasal verbs 1: Introduction
subtitle: get on / break down / take it off
summary: Understand what phrasal verbs are, how the second word can change the meaning, and where to put the object.

lesson.heading: What is a phrasal verb?
lesson.text: We often use verbs with words like **in, out, on, off, up, down, away, back, by, through, about, along, over, forward, round** or **around**. So you can say look out / get on / take off / run away etc. These are phrasal verbs. We often use on/off/out etc. with verbs of movement.

examples.text: The bus was full. We couldn't **get on**.
A woman got into the car and **drove off**.
Sarah is leaving tomorrow and **coming back** on Saturday.
When I touched him on the shoulder, he **turned round**.

lesson.heading: The second word often gives a special meaning
rows: Sorry I'm late. The car **broke down**.
I never **found out** who sent me the flowers.
It was my first flight. I was nervous as the plane **took off**.
I tried many times to contact her. In the end I **gave up**.
How was the exam? How did you **get on**?
My French isn't good, but it's enough to **get by**.

lesson.heading: Phrasal verb + preposition
lesson.text: Sometimes a phrasal verb is followed by a preposition: **look up at**, **run away from**, **keep up with**, **look forward to**.

examples.text: We **looked up at** the plane as it flew above us.
Why did you **run away from** me?
You're walking too fast. I can't **keep up with** you.
Are you **looking forward to** your trip?

lesson.heading: Phrasal verbs with an object
lesson.text: Sometimes a phrasal verb has an object. Usually there are two possible positions for the object: after the phrasal verb or between the two parts.

examples.text: I **turned on** the light. or I **turned** the light **on**.

left.label: Noun object: two positions
examples: I'm going to **take off** my shoes. or ... **take** my shoes **off**.
Don't **wake up** the baby. or Don't **wake** the baby **up**.
Don't **throw away** this box. or Don't **throw** this box **away**.

right.label: Pronoun object (it/them/me/him etc.): only one position
examples: These shoes are uncomfortable. I'm going to **take them off**. (not take off them)
The baby is asleep. Don't **wake her up**. (not wake up her)
I want to keep this box, so don't **throw it away**. (not throw away it)

lesson.text: A pronoun object always goes in the middle: turn **it** on, take **them** off, wake **her** up - never ~~turn on it~~.

exercises.prompt: Sorry I'm late. The car ___ on the way here, and we had to call for help.
exercises.explanation: break down = the engine stopped working.

exercises.prompt: I've been standing a long time. I'm going to ___ for a bit.
exercises.explanation: sit down - a verb of movement + down.

exercises.prompt: It's a very busy airport. There are planes landing and ___ all the time.
exercises.explanation: take off = go into the air (a plane).

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: make progress, do well or badly

exercises.prompt: A cat tried to catch the bird, but it ___ just in time.
exercises.explanation: fly away or fly off - both describe the movement of the bird leaving.

exercises.prompt: The meeting tomorrow is going to be difficult. I'm not looking ___ it.
exercises.explanation: look forward TO something = phrasal verb + preposition.

exercises.prompt: How do you know about the plan? How did you find ___ it?
exercises.explanation: find out about something = discover information about it.

exercises.prompt: I'm going to bed now. Ask someone to wake you at 6.30.
exercises.answer: Can you wake me up at 6.30?
exercises.explanation: The pronoun object (me) goes between the two parts: wake me up.

exercises.statement: These shoes are uncomfortable. I'm going to take off them.
exercises.explanation: I'm going to take them off. A pronoun object can only go between the two parts of the phrasal verb.

exercises.statement: These books are Lisa's. I have to give them back to her.
exercises.explanation: Correct. give them back - the pronoun object goes in the middle.

exercises.prompt: Does the second word simply show movement, or does it give the verb a special meaning?

items.text: The bus was full. We couldn't get on.
A woman got into the car and drove off.
Sorry I'm late. The car broke down.
I never found out who sent me the flowers.
When I touched him on the shoulder, he turned round.
In the end I gave up.
Sarah is coming back on Saturday.
My French is enough to get by.

exercises.prompt: My shoes are dirty. Say what you should do before going into the house.
exercises.answer: I'd better take them off before going into the house.
exercises.explanation: take them off - not take off them.
